title: Codec-controlled retrieval: conditional output laws and fixed-build profile leakage
contribution_type: conditional theory and reproducible implementation case study; journal submission
claim: For the studied zero-filled ribbon retrieval implementation and synthetic workload, a frozen output-count classifier distinguishes balanced and rare-minority stored-label profiles by repeatedly querying one fixed build. Conditional codec/window laws explain relevant structure but do not establish a calibrated model of the actual hash-derived sampler or general transcript privacy. Established random free-variable filling suppresses this classifier in the measured workload.
assumptions: The primary study stores labels 0, 1 and 2 on 5000 keys, with counts (1667,1667,1666) versus (4950,25,25), and canonical bytes 0,128,192.
The observer knows the two candidate profiles, codec, sizes, construction parameters and workload family; only decoded nonmember-output counts are classifier features.
The quoted primary endpoint uses 100000 distinct nonadaptive nonmember queries per build, a frozen binary64 rule and separately seeded evaluation keysets.
The global uniform-span model, independent-coefficient window model and actual coupled hash-derived sampler have distinct assumptions.

limitations: Finite synthetic workload and reproducible noncryptographic randomness; independent unit is the keyset, not each profile instance or query.
Actual hash sampling differs from the independent-coefficient reference; no joint/adaptive privacy guarantee or optimal-attacker claim.
Some transfer settings fail; chance accuracy for one classifier after random filling is not general privacy.
The original assignment-moment discrepancy remains unresolved and limits fresh-build representativeness.
Historical frozen classifier and binary64 boundary behavior remain unchanged; previously observed evaluation data are not unseen confirmation for retuned methods.
Exact submitted files, public source pins and an integrated-version archival DOI remain to be established.
